description: The WhatsApp operator routes (WhatsAppController, found by the V1-21b final repair with AuthGuard and BusinessGuard only) no longer leak or let any member change the business's sending identity. GET /whatsapp/businesses/:b/config answers no secret value to anyone: provider and fromNumber, and each credential (accessToken, authToken, accountSid) as {configured, last4}, last4 and phoneNumberId only for a member who may write the config. PATCH .../config is OWNER only (owner ruling D-11: the business profile, its sending identity and sibling business-config writes): the OWNER membership or Business.ownerId, plus the SUPER_ADMIN bypass, bound to the route's business; anyone else gets 403 {code:'BUSINESS_PROFILE_OWNER_ONLY'} (the code every D-11 writer answers) with the Business row byte-identical. A PATCH that omits a credential, sends it blank or mask-shaped, or echoes the GET view back keeps the stored ciphertext; a submitted credential that is already ciphertext (enc:v1:, e.g. another business's stored token) is refused 400 {code:'WHATSAPP_CREDENTIAL_CIPHERTEXT'} and a phoneNumberId another business holds (the shared webhook's routing key) is refused 409 {code:'WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID_IN_USE'}, nothing written, the claim serialised by an advisory lock on the id. POST send and POST messages need operations:write; GET status, conversations, conversations/:id, templates and POST test need operations:read (the module key KeyInboxController requires); the config owner (WhatsAppService.isConfigOwner, incl. a distinguished owner with no membership row) passes them too (WhatsAppOperationsScopeGuard). GET status carries phoneNumberId (as platformId) only to a config writer. A foreign business answers 403 with nothing written; the four webhook handlers are unchanged (no guards). No provider traffic: sends use the mock provider, global fetch is a failing recorder. R0-SEC2b-WHATSAPP-SECRET-READS extends it: the Business reads (GET /identity/businesses/:id, GET /identity/businesses and the PATCH response, all through sanitizeBusiness) answer metaData.whatsapp as {configured} only, to every reader, the owner included (no credential plaintext or ciphertext, no phoneNumberId); PATCH /identity/businesses/:id refuses a metaData.whatsapp key 400 {code:'BUSINESS_METADATA_KEY_RESERVED'} with nothing written (saveConfig is its only writer); the D-11 static guard lists metaData.whatsapp (D11W-09). Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/whatsapp-config-authority.integration.test.ts test/whatsapp.controller.test.ts src/core/config/d11-owner-writes.spec.ts
notes: The owner rule is restated in WhatsAppService.isConfigOwner (WhatsAppModule does not import IdentityModule), as TemplatesService.isProfileOwner, FinanceSettingsService and GmailService.assertConnectAuthority restate it: the OWNER membership, Business.ownerId and the SUPER_ADMIN platform bypass. PATCH config keeps AuthGuard + BusinessGuard and runs assertConfigOwner first; ModuleScopeGuard is not put on the config routes because it refuses a distinguished owner with no membership row (R0-CMF5 notes).

Module key: 'operations', the key every KeyInboxController route requires (WhatsApp inbound is ingested into the KEY inbox). Role defaults: STAFF operations:read (reads, no send), ADMIN and OWNER admin. The scoped routes run WhatsAppOperationsScopeGuard, a ModuleScopeGuard subclass that first admits WhatsAppService.isConfigOwner for the route's business (review CR-SEC2-1: ModuleScopeGuard alone refused the distinguished owner with no membership row the send and inbox routes, while PATCH config admitted it); everyone else gets ModuleScopeGuard's answer unchanged. The KEY inbox routes themselves still refuse that owner (ModuleScopeGuard, outside this write set).

phoneNumberId stays plain at rest: the shared webhook routes inbound by metaData.whatsapp.phoneNumberId. The three credentials stay encrypted with core/crypto/token-crypto encryptToken as before; a kept credential is the stored ciphertext, not re-encrypted.

R0-SEC2b: the d11-owner-writes static guard lists metaData.whatsapp in OWNER_ONLY_META_KEYS with WhatsAppService.saveConfig (guard assertConfigOwner) as its one writer, and pins that IdentityService.updateBusiness consults PROFILE_PATCH_RESERVED_META_KEYS before its write (D11W-09): the reader cannot see updateBusiness spreading the caller's metaData bag, so that half is pinned by name and proven on the real database by SEC2-T02/T06.

Review SEC2-R1: encryptToken returns an 'enc:v1:' value unchanged and one platform key decrypts every business's ciphertext, so saveConfig refuses submitted ciphertext; only plaintext or the business's own kept ciphertext is written. Closed by R0-SEC2b (SEC2-T02, SEC2-T06): PATCH /identity/businesses/:id, which merges the caller's metaData bag, refuses a metaData.whatsapp key (present at all, null and the masked read included) 400 BUSINESS_METADATA_KEY_RESERVED before anything is read or written; a non-owner still gets the D-11 owner refusal (403) first (SEC2-T07).

Review SEC2-R3: the phoneNumberId uniqueness check uses the shared webhook's own predicate (business.findFirst on metaData.whatsapp.phoneNumberId; the soft-delete extension excludes deleted businesses); re-saving the id the business already stores is never refused, so a duplicate that predates the check does not lock its holder out. Making the webhook lookup deterministic for such pre-existing duplicates is left to V1-21b (the webhook handlers are unchanged here, SEC2-H01/H02).

Follow-ups closed by R0-SEC2b: SEC2-T01/T04/T05 (review SEC2-R2: sanitizeBusiness masks metaData.whatsapp as {configured}), SEC2-T02/T06 (identity PATCH refuses metaData.whatsapp), SEC2-T03 (review CR-SEC2-2: the web WhatsApp page and the Key Connect manage drawer render a 403 from GET status as no access and read the masked status; proven in jsdom by apps/web/src/app/app/whatsapp/__tests__/whatsapp-status-access.test.tsx, which this server-side manifest cannot bind).

R0-SEC2b, not closed (outside its write set): Business.metaData also carries payment gateway secrets the web payments tab writes and reads back (stripeSecretKey, stripeWebhookSecret, paypalClientSecret, wipayApiKey); sanitizeBusiness masks only metaData.whatsapp, so GET /identity/businesses[/:id] still answers those to any member.
